questions.history: Use a UTC clock fixed at 2025-07-15T00:00:00Z. Compare the parent’s explicit trigger with both forms on the merge.
questions.prediction: The parent exposes the explicit form. The merge additionally accepts the three-argument call. Each supported form should retain one task whose next instant is 2025-07-15T08:00:00Z.
questions.basis: London observes UTC+01 on that date, so 09:00 London is 08:00 UTC. The PR describes the overload as equivalent to constructing the zoned trigger.
questions.refutation: The new overload fails to register, schedules a different instant, or disagrees with the explicit trigger.

questions.history: At the same UTC fixed clock register the existing two-argument addCronTask(task, expression). Make a second call with CRON_DISABLED ("-").
questions.prediction: Both revisions should retain only the original task, scheduled for 2025-07-15T09:00:00Z. On the merge the three-argument disabled call should likewise leave the list untouched.
questions.basis: With no explicit zone the trigger takes the context clock’s zone. The registrar documents "-" as disabling registration.
questions.refutation: The UTC task fires at 08:00Z, or the disabled call adds a task or throws.

questions.history: Keep the same London expression and override the trigger-context clock zone with Asia/Tokyo. Use the same initial instant as above, then a fresh history at 2025-01-15T00:00:00Z.
questions.prediction: All explicit-London forms on their supported revisions should still produce 08:00Z on July 15 and 09:00Z on January 15.
questions.basis: An explicit zone is independent of the clock’s display zone. London is UTC+01 in July and UTC+00 in January. A constant numeric offset cannot satisfy both.
questions.refutation: Changing only the clock zone moves the July instant, or the winter task still uses the summer offset.
